title: Build a VNode Renderer
short_description: Turn VNode trees into an object host and preserve their identity between renders.
description: The starter includes host operations for creating, inserting, moving, and removing nodes without depending on the real DOM.
Implement the renderer that mounts elements, updates props and children, processes components, and reconciles keyed lists.
instructions: Complete render(vnode, container) so it compares against container._vnode and also supports unmounting through null.
Complete patch(oldVNode, newVNode, container, anchor) so it replaces incompatible identities and dispatches Text, elements, and components.
Implement mountElement and patchElement with the operations from host.ts; key must not become a host prop.
Complete patchChildren so it handles transitions between text, arrays, and absence while unmounting what no longer exists.
Mount and update components by preserving an instance and patching the subtree returned by render(props).
Complete patchKeyedChildren so it reuses compatible type and key pairs, unmounts missing nodes, mounts new ones, and moves nodes into final order.
Keep resetRenderer working so every test can clear auxiliary state.

hints.title: Compatible identity
hints.body: Two VNodes can share a host node only when both `type` and `key` match. Before replacing, preserve the old node's next sibling as the anchor.

hints.title: Props and children
hints.body: Update new props first and then remove absent keys. For children, explicitly distinguish text, array, and null.

hints.title: Component subtree
hints.body: Store `{ vnode, subTree }` in `vnode.component`. On update, render with the new props and call `patch(previousTree, nextTree, ...)`.

hints.title: Keyed order
hints.body: Match VNodes by key first. Then walk the new list from right to left: the next VNode's `el` is the anchor used to mount or move the current one.
